title: Passive Voice Quiz 5
description: Every question hides a trap: two objects, intransitive verbs, rare structures or an unusual passive.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is the passive of 'She gave me a book', with the person as the subject?
questions.explanation: The person me becomes the subject I, and gave becomes was given. Watch out: was gave uses the past form after be.

questions.question: 'The accident was happened yesterday' is correct.
questions.explanation: Happen has no object, so it has no passive: The accident happened yesterday. Watch out: intransitive verbs are never used in the passive.

questions.question: It is believed that he escaped last night. = He {{1}} (believe) {{2}} (escape) last night.
questions.explanation: The impersonal passive becomes He is believed to have escaped, because the escape is earlier than the belief. Watch out: to escape would refer to the same time as the belief.

questions.question: I had my hair ___ yesterday.
questions.explanation: Have + object + past participle describes a service done for you, and the participle of cut is cut. Watch out: cut does not take -ed.

questions.question: Which sentence cannot be turned into the passive?
questions.explanation: Have meaning possession is a state verb and has no passive. Watch out: drives, bought and is selling all have objects and can be passive.

questions.question: Correct the mistake (past simple): The thieves were been arrested.
questions.explanation: The past simple passive is were + past participle, with no been. Watch out: been belongs to the perfect tenses.

questions.assertion: The passive of 'They are building a school' is 'A school is built'.
questions.reason: In the continuous tenses the passive adds being before the past participle.
questions.explanation: The reason is true, and it shows why the assertion is false: the passive of They are building a school is A school is being built. Watch out: is built alone would be the present simple passive.

questions.question: The report {{1}} (finish) by Friday. Use the future perfect passive.
questions.explanation: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle. Watch out: all three helpers are needed.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: The film is been shown now.
He is said to be a spy.
questions.explanation: The correct sentences use the impersonal passive, or be with a participle. Watch out: is been and repair are wrong forms after be and have.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The modal comes first, then have, then been, then the participle. Watch out: by Friday stays together at the end.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the get-passive?
questions.explanation: Get + past participle is an informal passive: The vase got broken. Watch out: did break and has broke are active forms, and was breaking is the past continuous.

questions.question: 'The prize was won by her' and 'She won the prize' describe the same event.
questions.explanation: Both describe the same fact, and only the focus changes. Watch out: the passive puts the prize first, so it stresses what happened to it.
